items.title: Govt to charge bulk Scotch imports 162.5% duty and tax amid UK pact standoff
items.summary: India has implemented a hefty 162.5% duty on bulk Scotch imports, surpassing previously established tariffs. This action follows a trade agreement with the UK that aimed to reduce Scotch tariffs to 75%. Investigators claim that Scotch imports are being misclassified, resulting in higher taxes on these goods. Major companies like Pernod Ricard and Diageo are facing disruptions due to blocked shipments at ports.

items.title: RBI may hike interest rates by 75 basis points by Q2 of next year: Goldman Sachs
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is projected to increase interest rates by 75 basis points by the second quarter of 2027. Analysts predict that headline inflation will remain above 6 percent into early 2027 before gradually decreasing. Despite the monetary tightening, India's GDP growth is expected to moderate to 7.2 percent in 2027. Strong domestic demand and an emerging investment cycle are likely to sustain economic activity.

items.title: Rupee ends flat after hitting seven-month high as firmer dollar offsets inflows
items.summary: The Indian rupee closed almost flat after peaking at a seven-month high during early trading on Wednesday. Robust foreign investments in local stocks provided a boost, but a stronger dollar capped further gains. The dollar index rose by 0.2%, reaching its highest since April 2025 due to anticipations of accelerated rate hikes.

items.title: Investigation into deadly Air India crash in final stage, govt says
items.summary: The Indian government has confirmed that its investigation into the Air India crash is nearing completion. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta presented updates to the Supreme Court, revealing that initial findings point to malfunctioning fuel-control switches as a factor in the engine failure. Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, the captain's father, expressed frustration over assumptions of pilot error. A final report is anticipated to be shared for commentary prior to its release.

items.title: Onion farmers seek measures to ensure Rs 3,000 per quintal amid surplus production outlook
items.summary: Maharashtra onion farmers have asked the Centre to ensure prices of at least Rs 3,000 per quintal by expanding export markets and maintaining a stable export policy, as India is expected to have a sizeable surplus in 2025-26. The growers’ body said better export infrastructure, storage, processing and transparent supply data will be critical to prevent price crashes when market arrivals rise.

The airline is focusing on rebuilding capacity and ensuring operational reliability going forward. The fundraising aims to strengthen its financial position and support fleet expansion efforts.

The company's stock market debut includes a fresh issue of 8 billion rupees and an offer for sale of shares. Aragen's current revenue largely comes from drug discovery services, with expectations of future growth.

The case involved a loan of Rs 3,250 crore given to Videocon Group during her tenure.

items.title: Reliance plans to invest about $1.6 billion to build new biogas plants
items.summary: Reliance Industries is set to invest about Rs 15,000 crore in the establishment of nearly 100 compressed biogas plants in India by 2030. With 45 biogas plants already in operation, Reliance plans a substantial increase by March 2027 to further support the nation's energy mix goals.

items.title: UPI and the trust pact in its second act
items.summary: As tap-and-pay, UPI AutoPay mandates and agentic commerce take hold, more payments in India will go through without a customer entering a PIN or approving each transaction. At a closed-door roundtable hosted by Mindgate Solutions with PayU, industry leaders examined what that shift demands of payment providers and merchants, and who pays for it. Read on for the trends to watch.

items.title: India, other major APAC nations to maintain strong prudential oversight: Moody's
items.summary: Moody's Ratings suggests that key Asia-Pacific countries are set to uphold strong prudential supervision, which acts as a bulwark against excessive risk-taking and reinforces banks' capital buffers. This stability projects a positive outlook for global banks in 2027, supported by resilient macroeconomic conditions that exhibit their adaptability in adverse circumstances. The upcoming year will see six defining themes influencing bank credit quality.

items.title: Mint Explainer: What FM's pre-budget stakeholder consultations mean
items.summary: Over the next few days, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman will huddle with industry executives, bankers, capital market participants, social sector experts, and, for the first time, young people and retired bureaucrats.

items.title: UPI’s free era is ending. Who pays, who earns, and who gets left behind?
items.summary: A slice of UPI is likely to stop being free in the future. At a closed-door roundtable in Bengaluru, the people who build, lend and collect on India’s favourite payments rail debated what this means for merchants, TPAPs and the economics of the ecosystem. Read on for the sharp insights.

items.title: Budget 2027: Economists oppose LTCG tax cut as industry seeks abolition; what they told Sitharaman
items.summary: Retain capital gains tax on equities, economists tell FM Sitharaman ahead of Budget 2027-28

items.title: Budget 2027: FM Sitharaman chairs third pre-Budget consultation with manufacturing sector leaders
items.summary: Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the third pre-Budget consultation meeting for the Union Budget 2027-28 in New Delhi. The meeting included representatives from the manufacturing sector and senior government officials providing suggestions. This exercise aims to gather inputs from various economic sectors to shape the Budget's priorities. The Union Budget is scheduled for presentation on February 1, 2027, along with the Economic Survey.

items.title: Air India, Airbus to develop voluntary corporate SAF programme
items.summary: Air India and Airbus are collaborating to develop a voluntary Sustainable Aviation Fuel programme for the aviation sector. The feasibility study will explore methods to reduce emissions linked to air travel. The Indian government plans to mandate a 1 percent blending of SAF in jet fuel by 2027. Investments of USD 70-85 billion are anticipated to support SAF production by 2040.

items.title: Odisha govt hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% for state employees
items.summary: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a three percent hike in Dearness Allowance for government employees. The increase raises the DA from 60 percent to 63 percent, effective from July 1. Pensioners will also benefit from the same three percent increase in Dearness Relief. Approximately 8.5 lakh government employees and pensioners will receive this additional financial support. Payments reflecting the increased DA will be included in the November salary.

items.title: Anil Agarwal warns ONGC's takeover of Vedanta's oilfield risks denting investor confidence
items.summary: Vedanta chairman Anil Agarwal has warned that the transfer of its producing Cambay offshore oil and gas block to ONGC could send the wrong signal to investors. Urging regulatory stability, Agarwal said Vedanta was committing $5 billion to boost oil and gas production. He called on the government to avoid disrupting existing operators as India seeks to cut energy imports.

items.title: JSW Steel CEO flags Chinese exports, trade barriers as key challenges
items.summary: JSW Steel's CEO Jayant Acharya highlighted the impact of Chinese steel exports on Indian steelmakers. He stated that tariff and non-tariff barriers in developed markets complicate the situation. Despite these challenges, domestic steel demand in India remains strong. Acharya emphasized the need for India to open more iron ore mines for adequate raw material supply. This initiative would support the future growth of the steel industry.

items.title: DRI searches Cipla's Mumbai office, Bhiwandi depot over imported drugs
items.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence's Mumbai zonal unit has searched Cipla's office in Vikhroli and its depot in Bhiwandi over the classification or exemption of an imported pharmaceutical finished product. Cipla said it cooperated with authorities and that the proceedings would have no material impact on its financials or operations.

items.title: Tata Steel seeks UK market support, Dutch green funds amid Chinese excessive supply: Narendran
items.summary: Tata Steel is seeking UK government intervention to address excess steel inventories and negotiating Dutch state funding for its green transition as Chinese oversupply, geopolitical conflicts and trade barriers disrupt global markets. CEO T V Narendran says the company is prioritising cost efficiency, value-added products and cleaner steelmaking to build resilience.

items.title: Budget 2027-28: Govt to invite Gen Z for pre-Budget consultations; Sitharaman meets economists
items.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has begun pre-Budget consultations with economists for the Union Budget 2027-28. The government will also seek inputs from industry, trade unions, state governments and other stakeholders.

items.title: SAF policy draft to be out in 2 weeks as India eyes $85 billion aviation fuel opportunity
items.summary: The government of India plans to release the draft sustainable aviation fuel policy for public commentary soon. This initiative aims to enhance local production and reduce the country's reliance on fuel imports. Approximately 10 million tonnes of sustainable aviation fuel could be produced annually by 2040. The policy will support only indigenously manufactured fuel to blend with Aviation Turbine Fuel.

items.title: IL&FS crisis was India's Lehman moment, swift action helped contain contagion: Uday Kotak
items.summary: Uday Kotak has described the 2018 IL&FS crisis as India's Lehman Brothers moment, warning that the collapse could have triggered widespread contagion across the financial sector. He credited swift government intervention and coordination with regulators and stakeholders for containing the crisis. IL&FS had 340 companies and defaulted on over Rs 91,000 crore despite holding a triple-A rating.

items.title: Japan proposes ‘Asian IEA’ to manage oil stockpiles
items.summary: Tokyo hopes joint reserves would insulate import-dependent region against future energy shocks

items.title: India's CAD may touch 1.2% of GDP in FY27 as oil, gold demand pose risks: UBI
items.summary: India's current account deficit is projected to reach 1.2% of GDP in FY27, driven by oil prices, according to a report by Union Bank of India. The report emphasizes that high crude oil prices and gold demand could impact the external balance. Merchandise trade deficit widened to a significant USD 39.88 billion in October. Additionally, imports surged while services trade surplus remained nearly flat during the same period.

items.title: Midterm Meltdown: How US elections sparked a rethink on energy risks
items.summary: Energy markets from crude oil and diesel to natural gas, LNG, coal and tanker freight have declined since the US midterm elections, suggesting traders are pricing in a lower risk of wider conflict in the Middle East. However, Europe's low gas inventories and potential supply disruptions remain significant risks.

items.title: How Jensen Huang scandal makes Congress a bigger risk to U.S.-China relations
items.summary: Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a woman suspected by the U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy has spurred efforts seeking stricter curbs on tech exports to Beijing.

items.summary: On recent USD strength

Jay-Z backed music rights firm raises nearly $700mn to expand portfolio
items.summary: Fundraising is the latest to be backed by a securitisation of music royalties as investors look for steady yields outside of traditional markets

items.title: Banks seek to curb AI debt exposure as backlash mounts
items.summary: Lenders are offloading debt tied to data centres and chips as public opposition threatens to derail mega projects

items.title: Rothschild & Co anchors Italy at heart of European growth plan
items.summary: Family-run bank targets country’s new fortunes as part of push to surpass €200bn in wealth and asset management assets by 2030

items.title: India Inc.’s sudden craving for dollars is a dangerous gamble
items.summary: India's increasing reliance on US dollar borrowing poses potential risks for future financial stability and currency strength. The Reserve Bank of India has promoted overseas dollar raising, but this could lead to vulnerabilities. Strengthening dollar reserves through debt might not address underlying economic issues effectively.

items.title: Centre hikes windfall tax on diesel, ATF exports; petrol levy unchanged — Check details
items.summary: This follows the previous revision on October 31, when the government raised the diesel export levy from ₹8.5 to ₹11.5 per litre and the ATF duty from ₹10.5 to ₹11 per litre, while completely scrapping a ₹2.5 per litre levy on petrol exports.

items.title: Wholesale inflation faces a triple squeeze from fuel, food and metals in FY27: Report
items.summary: India's wholesale inflation is currently anticipated to reach around 11 percent in FY27, surpassing earlier projections. Persistent pressures from energy and input costs alongside risks to food prices are significant factors. The report highlights that global commodity prices will greatly influence this inflation trajectory. A potential 25-basis-point rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India is also expected in December.

items.title: Nasdaq 100 sinks 2.7% in gloomy start to pivotal week for AI trade
items.summary: US chip stocks fall as Nvidia sustains fresh bout of selling pressure

items.title: Egypt, India aim to hit $12 bn bilateral trade target within five years, says Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty
items.summary: Egypt and India are aiming to increase bilateral trade to $12 billion over the next five years and expand Indian investment in the North African country, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said. The target was discussed during Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's visit to Egypt with an Indian business delegation.

items.title: We couldn't afford a house alone, so we bought one with strangers
items.summary: People who can't afford to get on the housing ladder are buying homes with someone they don't know.

items.title: India's economic strength underpins attractive investment climate: Nirmala Sitharaman
items.summary: "The USISPF Board reiterated its commitment to investing in India, including in R&D, reflecting confidence in India's growth story and innovation ecosystem," the Finance Ministry said in a post on X.

items.title: India-EU should ensure maximum utilisation of FTA: Ambassador Jean-Eric Paquet
items.summary: The agreement will not only ensure that trade flourishes but also will open new opportunities, including those in research and innovation, with Assam poised to benefit from it, he said.

items.title: India's sugar output more than doubles to 23.59 lakh tonnes by November 15
items.summary: India has seen a significant rise in sugar production, reaching 23.59 lakh tonnes by November 15. This increase is attributed mainly to the early start of crushing operations in Maharashtra. Sugar mills in Maharashtra rose to 154, contributing 18.51 lakh tonnes of sugar production. Other states like Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka are gradually boosting their crushing activities.
